# `kernel/ai-hub/SmartModelPolicy.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/ai-hub/SmartModelPolicy.js`

SmartModelPolicy.js - deterministic policy and catalog ranking for AI Hub. This module performs no provider calls, stores no credentials, and grants no authority. It projects provider catalog records into an inspectable ranking that Navi cognition can compile into its existing signed route contract.

## Functions

### `classifySmartModelRouterAlias(provider, model)`

Classify provider-side router aliases separately from concrete model IDs. Dynamic aliases may resolve to a different model on every request, so their catalog capabilities cannot safely authorize strict or effectful tasks.

### `classifySmartModelRole(raw = {})`

Classify whether one endpoint can participate in general Navi cognition. Explicit specialist capabilities, role metadata, and non-text output roles win first. Strong canonical specialist identities win next because providers may label a guard classifier with a generic pipeline such as `image-text-to-text`. Affirmative general metadata is considered only after those exclusions. Unknown endpoints retain compatibility eligibility but are reported distinctly from evidenced general-cognition models.

### `isSmartModelGeneralCognitionEligible(raw = {})`

Unknown endpoints retain legacy eligibility; evidenced specialists do not.

### `defaultSmartModelPolicy()`

Return a detached, immutable basic policy suitable for persisted settings.

### `normalizeSmartModelPolicy(raw = null)`

Normalize persisted policy. Missing fields migrate to v1 defaults, while an unknown field or version is rejected so misspelled safety controls never silently disappear.

### `normalizeSmartModelPreference(raw = null)`

Normalize one content-free operator model preference. Preferences improve ranking only; they never approve a route or relax an eligibility gate.

### `resolveSmartModelPreference({ text = '', models = [], selectedModels = [] } = {})`

Parse only the current operator-authored turn into a bounded preference. Catalog labels, descriptions, and provider-supplied aliases are deliberately ignored: only canonical provider/model identifiers can produce a target.

### `smartModelPreferenceAffinity(preference, provider, model)`

Return the exact bounded affinity for one canonical route, if resolved.

### `inferSmartModelWorkloadProfile(raw = {})`

Infer preference-only workload affinities from one provider catalog row. The result improves ranking and model-picker explanations. It is never an authorization claim: privacy, modality, tool transport, context, endpoint health, and budget remain separate hard eligibility checks.

### `classifySmartModelTask(raw = {})`

Classify a task without consulting a model. Explicit purpose wins; otherwise bounded, ordered rules use declared modality/privacy/background state before keyword signals. Raw user text is never copied into the returned evidence.

### `normalizeSmartModelCandidate(raw)`

Project one provider-catalog record into the policy's provider-neutral form.

### `estimateSmartModelCostMicrounits(candidate, estimatedTokens)`

Conservative projected cost for a normalized candidate and token estimate.

### `rankSmartModelPool({ policy: rawPolicy = null, models = [], task = {}, usage = null } = {})`

Rank a catalog and return a deterministic, inspectable decision. The caller still owns provider authentication, canonical resource reservations, and final execution authority.

### `selectSmartModelPool(options = {})`

Semantic alias for callers that consume the selected route and fallbacks.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
